views.name: player_latest_attributes
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  player_fifa_api_id,
  player_api_id,
  date,
  overall_rating,
  potential,
  preferred_foot,
  attacking_work_rate,
  defensive_work_rate,
  crossing,
  finishing,
  heading_accuracy,
  short_passing,
  volleys,
  dribbling,
  curve,
  free_kick_accuracy,
  long_passing,
  ball_control,
  acceleration,
  sprint_speed,
  agility,
  reactions,
  balance,
  shot_power,
  jumping,
  stamina,
  strength,
  long_shots,
  aggression,
  interceptions,
  positioning,
  vision,
  penalties,
  marking,
  standing_tackle,
  sliding_tackle,
  gk_diving,
  gk_handling,
  gk_kicking,
  gk_positioning,
  gk_reflexes,
  row_number AS latest_attr_rank
FROM (
  SELECT
    pa.*,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY player_api_id ORDER BY date DESC, id DESC) AS row_number
  FROM Player_Attributes pa
) sub
WHERE row_number = 1

params.description: One-row-per-player view returning the most recent player attribute record (by date, tie-broken by id) for each player_api_id.
params.when_to_use: Get the latest known attributes/ratings for a player (e.g., current overall_rating, potential, skills). | Join player identity or roster tables to show current attributes alongside player metadata. | Compose player-level aggregates where each player should contribute at most one latest record (e.g., average latest overall_rating by team or nation). | Filter players by recent attribute values (e.g., find players with latest potential >= X).
params.output_schema: id: primary key of the selected Player_Attributes row (Player_Attributes.id). | player_fifa_api_id: FIFA-side player id from Player_Attributes.player_fifa_api_id. | player_api_id: internal player id from Player_Attributes.player_api_id — this view's grain (one row per player_api_id). | date: date of the attribute snapshot from Player_Attributes.date (the latest snapshot for the player). | overall_rating: overall_rating from Player_Attributes (numeric rating at that snapshot). | potential: potential from Player_Attributes (numeric). | preferred_foot: preferred_foot from Player_Attributes (string). | attacking_work_rate: attacking_work_rate from Player_Attributes (string). | defensive_work_rate: defensive_work_rate from Player_Attributes (string). | crossing: crossing from Player_Attributes (numeric skill). | finishing: finishing from Player_Attributes (numeric). | heading_accuracy: heading_accuracy from Player_Attributes (numeric). | short_passing: short_passing from Player_Attributes (numeric). | volleys: volleys from Player_Attributes (numeric). | dribbling: dribbling from Player_Attributes (numeric). | curve: curve from Player_Attributes (numeric). | free_kick_accuracy: free_kick_accuracy from Player_Attributes (numeric). | long_passing: long_passing from Player_Attributes (numeric). | ball_control: ball_control from Player_Attributes (numeric). | acceleration: acceleration from Player_Attributes (numeric). | sprint_speed: sprint_speed from Player_Attributes (numeric). | agility: agility from Player_Attributes (numeric). | reactions: reactions from Player_Attributes (numeric). | balance: balance from Player_Attributes (numeric). | shot_power: shot_power from Player_Attributes (numeric). | jumping: jumping from Player_Attributes (numeric). | stamina: stamina from Player_Attributes (numeric). | strength: strength from Player_Attributes (numeric). | long_shots: long_shots from Player_Attributes (numeric). | aggression: aggression from Player_Attributes (numeric). | interceptions: interceptions from Player_Attributes (numeric). | positioning: positioning from Player_Attributes (numeric). | vision: vision from Player_Attributes (numeric). | penalties: penalties from Player_Attributes (numeric). | marking: marking from Player_Attributes (numeric). | standing_tackle: standing_tackle from Player_Attributes (numeric). | sliding_tackle: sliding_tackle from Player_Attributes (numeric). | gk_diving: gk_diving from Player_Attributes (numeric). | gk_handling: gk_handling from Player_Attributes (numeric). | gk_kicking: gk_kicking from Player_Attributes (numeric). | gk_positioning: gk_positioning from Player_Attributes (numeric). | gk_reflexes: gk_reflexes from Player_Attributes (numeric). | latest_attr_rank: row_number assigned by ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY player_api_id ORDER BY date DESC, id DESC). Always = 1 in this view.
params.grounded_columns: Player_Attributes.id | Player_Attributes.player_fifa_api_id | Player_Attributes.player_api_id | Player_Attributes.date | Player_Attributes.overall_rating | Player_Attributes.potential | Player_Attributes.preferred_foot | Player_Attributes.attacking_work_rate | Player_Attributes.defensive_work_rate | Player_Attributes.crossing | Player_Attributes.finishing | Player_Attributes.heading_accuracy | Player_Attributes.short_passing | Player_Attributes.volleys | Player_Attributes.dribbling | Player_Attributes.curve | Player_Attributes.free_kick_accuracy | Player_Attributes.long_passing | Player_Attributes.ball_control | Player_Attributes.acceleration | Player_Attributes.sprint_speed | Player_Attributes.agility | Player_Attributes.reactions | Player_Attributes.balance | Player_Attributes.shot_power | Player_Attributes.jumping | Player_Attributes.stamina | Player_Attributes.strength | Player_Attributes.long_shots | Player_Attributes.aggression | Player_Attributes.interceptions | Player_Attributes.positioning | Player_Attributes.vision | Player_Attributes.penalties | Player_Attributes.marking | Player_Attributes.standing_tackle | Player_Attributes.sliding_tackle | Player_Attributes.gk_diving | Player_Attributes.gk_handling | Player_Attributes.gk_kicking | Player_Attributes.gk_positioning | Player_Attributes.gk_reflexes | sub.row_number
params.metric: latest_attr_rank = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY Player_Attributes.player_api_id ORDER BY Player_Attributes.date DESC, Player_Attributes.id DESC) -- ranking expression used to pick the latest row; filtered to = 1 in this view
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to player_identity on player_latest_attributes.player_api_id = player_identity.player_api_id — safe because player_latest_attributes has exactly one row per player_api_id, so attributes are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to team_latest_attributes only after joining player -> team at a one-to-one level (e.g., if you have a single team_id per player for a snapshot). Joining player_latest_attributes directly to team_latest_attributes on team-level keys is safe only if the join path is one-to-one; otherwise aggregate after the join. | do NOT directly join player_latest_attributes to a one-to-many table/view such as match_lineup_players_unpivot or match_basic_outcomes without re-aggregation or restricting the many-side: those views contain multiple rows per player (matches, lineups, outcomes) and would multiply this view's one-row-per-player measures. If you need player-level aggregates of match data, first aggregate the many-side to one row per player (e.g., COUNT(matches) or AVG(metric) grouped by player_api_id) and then join. | If composing team- or match-level metrics from this view, ensure you aggregate player_latest_attributes after joining if the target grain is team or match (e.g., AVG(overall_rating) GROUP BY team_id). Do not assume team-level uniqueness unless you join via a one-to-one relationship (explicit team assignment table/view). | When joining to sibling aggregated views (e.g., match_team_odds or team_latest_attributes), verify their grains. Joining two one-row-per-entity views on that entity's key (e.g., player_api_id to player_api_id) is safe; joining one-row-per-player (this view) to one-row-per-team (team view) is many-to-one (safe for preserving player rows) but will duplicate team measures per player if you expect a single team row — if you want team measures only once, aggregate players or select distinct team rows instead.

views.description: For each player (player_api_id), pick the most recent Player_Attributes snapshot by date and expose key ratings. Useful when you need a single canonical rating row per player for joins or aggregations (e.g., top players by overall_rating, join player attributes to matches or teams). | Use for: Find top-N players by overall_rating; Join latest player ratings to matches' lineups; Compute average attribute by team using latest player snapshots

views.name: team_latest_attributes
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  team_fifa_api_id,
  team_api_id,
  date,
  buildUpPlaySpeed,
  buildUpPlaySpeedClass,
  buildUpPlayDribbling,
  buildUpPlayDribblingClass,
  buildUpPlayPassing,
  buildUpPlayPassingClass,
  buildUpPlayPositioningClass,
  chanceCreationPassing,
  chanceCreationPassingClass,
  chanceCreationCrossing,
  chanceCreationCrossingClass,
  chanceCreationShooting,
  chanceCreationShootingClass,
  chanceCreationPositioningClass,
  defencePressure,
  defencePressureClass,
  defenceAggression,
  defenceAggressionClass,
  defenceTeamWidth,
  defenceTeamWidthClass,
  defenceDefenderLineClass,
  row_number AS latest_team_attr_rank
FROM (
  SELECT
    ta.*,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY team_api_id ORDER BY date DESC, id DESC) AS row_number
  FROM Team_Attributes ta
) sub
WHERE row_number = 1

params.description: Provides the latest (most recent date) Team_Attributes record per team_api_id — one row per team_api_id with the most recent attributes and a rank marker.
params.when_to_use: Get the current/latest tactical/attribute snapshot for a team (e.g., latest buildUpPlaySpeed, defencePressure) for display or enrichment. | Join latest team attributes into match- or player-level datasets when you need the most recent team-level attributes as of the team's latest recorded date. | Compose metrics that compare current team attributes across teams (rankings, filters, summary stats). | Use as a dimension-like source to filter or group by the latest attribute classes (e.g., buildUpPlaySpeedClass) without duplicating attribute rows.
params.output_schema: id: primary key of the Team_Attributes record (derived from Team_Attributes.id) | team_fifa_api_id: FIFA identifier for the team (derived from Team_Attributes.team_fifa_api_id) | team_api_id: internal team identifier — the view's grain (derived from Team_Attributes.team_api_id) | date: date of the Team_Attributes record — used for determining latest row (derived from Team_Attributes.date) | buildUpPlaySpeed: numeric score for build-up play speed (derived from Team_Attributes.buildUpPlaySpeed) | buildUpPlaySpeedClass: categorical class for build-up play speed (derived from Team_Attributes.buildUpPlaySpeedClass) | buildUpPlayDribbling: numeric score for build-up play dribbling (derived from Team_Attributes.buildUpPlayDribbling) | buildUpPlayDribblingClass: categorical class for build-up play dribbling (derived from Team_Attributes.buildUpPlayDribblingClass) | buildUpPlayPassing: numeric score for build-up play passing (derived from Team_Attributes.buildUpPlayPassing) | buildUpPlayPassingClass: categorical class for build-up play passing (derived from Team_Attributes.buildUpPlayPassingClass) | buildUpPlayPositioningClass: categorical class for build-up play positioning (derived from Team_Attributes.buildUpPlayPositioningClass) | chanceCreationPassing: numeric chance-creation passing score (derived from Team_Attributes.chanceCreationPassing) | chanceCreationPassingClass: categorical class for chance-creation passing (derived from Team_Attributes.chanceCreationPassingClass) | chanceCreationCrossing: numeric chance-creation crossing score (derived from Team_Attributes.chanceCreationCrossing) | chanceCreationCrossingClass: categorical class for chance-creation crossing (derived from Team_Attributes.chanceCreationCrossingClass) | chanceCreationShooting: numeric chance-creation shooting score (derived from Team_Attributes.chanceCreationShooting) | chanceCreationShootingClass: categorical class for chance-creation shooting (derived from Team_Attributes.chanceCreationShootingClass) | chanceCreationPositioningClass: categorical class for chance-creation positioning (derived from Team_Attributes.chanceCreationPositioningClass) | defencePressure: numeric defence pressure score (derived from Team_Attributes.defencePressure) | defencePressureClass: categorical class for defence pressure (derived from Team_Attributes.defencePressureClass) | defenceAggression: numeric defence aggression score (derived from Team_Attributes.defenceAggression) | defenceAggressionClass: categorical class for defence aggression (derived from Team_Attributes.defenceAggressionClass) | defenceTeamWidth: numeric defence team width score (derived from Team_Attributes.defenceTeamWidth) | defenceTeamWidthClass: categorical class for defence team width (derived from Team_Attributes.defenceTeamWidthClass) | defenceDefenderLineClass: categorical class for defender line (derived from Team_Attributes.defenceDefenderLineClass) | latest_team_attr_rank: integer row_number per team_api_id ordered by date desc, id desc — equals 1 for the row included (derived from ROW_NUMBER() window over Team_Attributes partitioned by team_api_id)
params.grounded_columns: Team_Attributes.id | Team_Attributes.team_fifa_api_id | Team_Attributes.team_api_id | Team_Attributes.date | Team_Attributes.buildUpPlaySpeed | Team_Attributes.buildUpPlaySpeedClass | Team_Attributes.buildUpPlayDribbling | Team_Attributes.buildUpPlayDribblingClass | Team_Attributes.buildUpPlayPassing | Team_Attributes.buildUpPlayPassingClass | Team_Attributes.buildUpPlayPositioningClass | Team_Attributes.chanceCreationPassing | Team_Attributes.chanceCreationPassingClass | Team_Attributes.chanceCreationCrossing | Team_Attributes.chanceCreationCrossingClass | Team_Attributes.chanceCreationShooting | Team_Attributes.chanceCreationShootingClass | Team_Attributes.chanceCreationPositioningClass | Team_Attributes.defencePressure | Team_Attributes.defencePressureClass | Team_Attributes.defenceAggression | Team_Attributes.defenceAggressionClass | Team_Attributes.defenceTeamWidth | Team_Attributes.defenceTeamWidthClass | Team_Attributes.defenceDefenderLineClass
params.metric: latest_team_attr_rank = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY Team_Attributes.team_api_id ORDER BY Team_Attributes.date DESC, Team_Attributes.id DESC)  -- window-based rank; view filters where = 1 | All other columns are passthroughs (no aggregation) from the selected Team_Attributes row; e.g., buildUpPlaySpeed = Team_Attributes.buildUpPlaySpeed
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to team identity/dimension views on team_api_id — e.g., join to player_identity or any team dimension keyed by team_api_id — safe because team_latest_attributes is one-row-per-team_api_id (its rows will not be duplicated): JOIN team_latest_attributes tla ON tla.team_api_id = dim.team_api_id | safe to join to match-level tables only when the join key is one-to-one per match-team, using match-team keys (match_id + team_api_id) and ensuring match-level rows are unique per team; if match table is one-row-per-team per match, joining on (match_id, team_api_id) is safe because team_latest_attributes remains one row per team and will not multiply measures | do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables (e.g., match events, lineups unpivoted, or player tables) on team_api_id without aggregation or deduplication, because those one-to-many relationships will multiply team_latest_attributes rows/measures. Instead: | - When joining to match_lineup_players_unpivot (one-to-many: many players per team per match), aggregate the players side first (e.g., COUNT, AVG) to one row per match+team, then join on (match_id, team_api_id). | - When combining with player_latest_attributes or player_identity, perform the join on player keys when you need player-level rows (accepts multiplication), or pre-aggregate player measures to team level before joining if you want to preserve team-level cardinality. | When composing metrics across time (e.g., attributes as of a match date), this view always returns the latest recorded attribute overall; it is NOT time-travel aware. To avoid temporal mismatch, either filter Team_Attributes by date before taking latest (create a time-bounded view) or join on date-aware keys (e.g., use Team_Attributes directly with date constraints) — otherwise you may incorrectly attribute post-match recorded attributes to earlier matches. | Because the view selects the single ROW_NUMBER()=1 record per team_api_id, joins on team_api_id to dimension tables keyed by team_api_id are safe and will not duplicate measures; any join to tables with multiple rows per team_api_id must be preceded by aggregation/deduplication on that side.

views.description: For each team (team_api_id), return the most recent Team_Attributes snapshot by date including numeric and class fields. Use when you need a single current team profile per team for analysis or joins (e.g., compare team tactics vs match outcomes). | Use for: Join team tactical profiles to matches; Compare teams by buildUpPlaySpeed or chanceCreation metrics; Aggregate team attributes across a league

views.name: match_lineup_players_unpivot
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS id,
  match_api_id AS match_api_id,
  'home' AS side,
  home_team_api_id AS team_api_id,
  home_player_1 AS player_api_id,
  1 AS lineup_slot
FROM Match
WHERE home_player_1 IS NOT NULL
UNION ALL
SELECT id, match_api_id, 'home', home_team_api_id, home_player_2, 2 FROM Match WHERE home_player_2 IS NOT NULL
UNION ALL

params.description: An unpivoted roster of match lineups: one row per match, team side, lineup slot and player (home and away), suitable for joining players/teams to match-level data or aggregating per player-slot across matches.
params.when_to_use: Find which player occupied a specific lineup slot for a match (e.g., who was home player in slot 7 for match id X). | Aggregate player participation counts across matches (e.g., how many matches did player P start in any slot, or in a specific slot). | Join per-player attributes (from player_identity or player_latest_attributes) to match-level lineup information. | Join team attributes (from team_latest_attributes) to the team in a match-side lineup row. | Compose match-level outcomes or odds (from match_basic_outcomes or match_team_odds) with the per-player lineup to analyze outcomes by lineup membership.
params.output_schema: id: match row identifier from Match.id. This is the base match table primary key that identifies the match containing the lineup. | match_api_id: match API id from Match.match_api_id (same as id in many contexts), provided to preserve original match identifier present in Match. | side: string literal 'home' or 'away' indicating the team side for this lineup row. In this view only 'home' rows are present (see grounded_columns). | team_api_id: team identifier for the side in the match derived from Match.home_team_api_id (the team that owns the listed home_player_X slots). | player_api_id: player identifier occupying the lineup slot, derived from the corresponding Match.home_player_N column (home_player_1 ... home_player_11). | lineup_slot: integer lineup slot number (1..11) derived from the literal values in each UNION branch representing which home_player_N column supplied player_api_id.
params.grounded_columns: Match.id | Match.match_api_id | Match.home_team_api_id | Match.home_player_1 | Match.home_player_2 | Match.home_player_3 | Match.home_player_4 | Match.home_player_5 | Match.home_player_6 | Match.home_player_7 | Match.home_player_8 | Match.home_player_9 | Match.home_player_10 | Match.home_player_11
params.metric: This view does not define aggregated numeric metrics. It provides descriptive columns at the grain (id, player_api_id, lineup_slot). | Derived boolean/non-NULL filter semantics: row exists iff the corresponding Match.home_player_N IS NOT NULL (i.e., participation in that slot).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to player_identity on player_api_id — safe because player_identity is (or should be) one-row-per-player_api_id (a dimension). Joining on match_lineup_players_unpivot.player_api_id = player_identity.player_api_id will not duplicate lineup rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to player_latest_attributes on player_api_id — safe when player_latest_attributes is implemented as one-row-per-player (RANK semantic). This preserves one row per lineup entry. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to team_latest_attributes on team_api_id — safe because team_latest_attributes is a team-dimension (one-row-per-team_api_id). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to match_basic_outcomes on Match.id or match_api_id — safe because match_basic_outcomes is normalized to one-row-per-match (NORM). This attaches match-level measures to each lineup row; note that match-level metrics will be duplicated across all lineup rows for that match by design (one lineup row per player), which is correct if you intend per-player participation with match context. | unsafe / cautionary guidance: do NOT join this view directly to any one-to-many fact that contains multiple rows per (match,id) or per (player_api_id,match) without first aggregating the many-side, because such joins will multiply the number of lineup rows and therefore multiply any measures derived from this view. Examples: |  - Do NOT directly join to match_team_odds if match_team_odds contains multiple odds rows per match/team (AGG vs raw) unless you aggregate odds to one row per match+team first. Otherwise odds rows will duplicate lineup rows for that team within the same match. |  - Do NOT directly join to any event/possession or substitution table that has multiple rows per match+player without aggregating/subselecting, because it will multiply counts when computing measures like participation counts. | composition patterns to preserve correctness: |  - To compute per-player counts of matches started: SELECT player_api_id, COUNT(*) FROM match_lineup_players_unpivot GROUP BY player_api_id; |  - To compute per-player match outcomes (win/loss) safely: join match_basic_outcomes (one-row-per-match) on id, then aggregate by player_api_id. This is safe because match_basic_outcomes is one-row-per-match; duplication only arises from the intended lineup multiplicity (one row per player in a match). |  - To combine with a many-row table (e.g., events) aggregate the many-side to the same grain (id, player_api_id) before joining, or aggregate the joined result afterwards using GROUP BY (id, player_api_id) to avoid measure inflation.

views.description: Unpivot Match lineup columns (home_player_1..11 and away_player_1..11) into one row per match-player appearance. Exposes match id, match_api_id, team side (home/away), team_api_id, player_api_id and lineup_slot. Useful when counting appearances, joining player info to appearances, or analyzing player presence per match. | Use for: Count appearances by player or team; Join player attributes to each appearance; Filter matches where a specific player appeared

views.name: match_basic_outcomes
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  match_api_id,
  country_id,
  league_id,
  season,
  stage,
  date,
  home_team_api_id,
  away_team_api_id,
  home_team_goal,
  away_team_goal,
  (home_team_goal - away_team_goal) AS goal_difference,
  CASE
    WHEN home_team_goal > away_team_goal THEN 'home_win'
    WHEN home_team_goal = away_team_goal THEN 'draw'
    WHEN home_team_goal < away_team_goal THEN 'away_win'
  END AS match_result,
  B365H,
  B365D,
  B365A
FROM Match

params.description: Provides one-row-per-match basic outcomes and closing odds (score, result, goal difference, and Bet365 closing odds) for matches in the Match table.
params.when_to_use: Get match-level outcome (winner/draw), scoreline, and goal difference for reporting or labeling tasks (e.g., training match outcome models). | Combine match outcomes with team or player attributes to analyze how attributes relate to match results (must respect cardinality guidance). | Join match-level betting odds (B365H/B365D/B365A) with outcomes for betting-performance or calibration analyses. | Filter or aggregate match outcomes by country, league, season, date, stage, or teams (home/away).
params.output_schema: id: Primary key of the match row (Match.id). Unique identifier for this match. | match_api_id: External API identifier for the match (Match.match_api_id). | country_id: Identifier for the country where the match took place (Match.country_id). | league_id: Identifier for the league this match belongs to (Match.league_id). | season: Season label for the match (Match.season). | stage: Stage/round of the competition for the match (Match.stage). | date: Match date (Match.date). | home_team_api_id: API identifier for the home team (Match.home_team_api_id). | away_team_api_id: API identifier for the away team (Match.away_team_api_id). | home_team_goal: Home team's goals scored in the match (Match.home_team_goal). | away_team_goal: Away team's goals scored in the match (Match.away_team_goal). | goal_difference: home_team_goal - away_team_goal (computed from Match.home_team_goal and Match.away_team_goal). Positive => home scored more. | match_result: Categorical result computed as: 'home_win' if home_team_goal > away_team_goal, 'draw' if equal, 'away_win' if home_team_goal < away_team_goal (derived from Match.home_team_goal and Match.away_team_goal). | B365H: Closing home-win decimal odds from Bet365 (Match.B365H). | B365D: Closing draw decimal odds from Bet365 (Match.B365D). | B365A: Closing away-win decimal odds from Bet365 (Match.B365A).
params.grounded_columns: Match.id | Match.match_api_id | Match.country_id | Match.league_id | Match.season | Match.stage | Match.date | Match.home_team_api_id | Match.away_team_api_id | Match.home_team_goal | Match.away_team_goal | Match.B365H | Match.B365D | Match.B365A
params.metric: goal_difference = (Match.home_team_goal - Match.away_team_goal) | match_result = CASE WHEN Match.home_team_goal > Match.away_team_goal THEN 'home_win' WHEN Match.home_team_goal = Match.away_team_goal THEN 'draw' WHEN Match.home_team_goal < Match.away_team_goal THEN 'away_win' END | Note: B365H, B365D, B365A are passed through raw from Match (no aggregation).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to team_latest_attributes(RANK) on match_basic_outcomes.home_team_api_id = team_latest_attributes.team_api_id — safe because team_latest_attributes is one-row-per-team (ranked/latest) so it will not multiply match rows and match-level measures remain intact. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to team_latest_attributes(RANK) on match_basic_outcomes.away_team_api_id = team_latest_attributes.team_api_id — safe for same reason as above when using the latest/one-row-per-team view. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to player_identity(JOIN) only when joining via a one-to-one key (e.g., if you have a single player id column on the match row). Do NOT join directly to player_identity on team/player keys that are many-to-one without first aggregating player_identity to one row per key, otherwise match rows will be duplicated. | DO NOT join directly to match_lineup_players_unpivot(RESHAPE) without re-aggregation: match_lineup_players_unpivot is many-rows-per-match (one row per lineup player). Joining it directly will duplicate match_basic_outcomes rows and multiply match-level measures (scores/odds). If you need per-match aggregates of lineups (e.g., count of starters), pre-aggregate match_lineup_players_unpivot to one row per match (e.g., GROUP BY match id) before joining. | DO NOT join directly to match_team_odds(AGG) unless you ensure keys align and match_team_odds is one-row-per-match: if match_team_odds is aggregated to one row per match it is safe; if it contains multiple odds rows per match (e.g., multiple bookmakers or timestamps), join only after aggregating to a single row per match (e.g., latest odds per match) to avoid duplicating match measures. | When composing further aggregates on top of this view (e.g., average goal_difference by team), aggregate at the match_basic_outcomes level (GROUP BY the dimension) rather than joining to a table with many children per match, or use DISTINCT match id in downstream joins to preserve one-row-per-match semantics. | If you need to join to any table/view that is naturally one-to-many with Match (players, events, lineups, odds history), transform that table first into a single-row-per-match summary (aggregation, filtering to most relevant row) before joining to this view so measures (goal_difference, B365*) are not inadvertently multiplied.

views.description: Normalized projection of Match with canonical outcome columns and basic betting odds selection. Computes match outcome (home_win/draw/away_win) and goal difference. Useful as a clean starting point for match-level modeling or aggregation. | Use for: Aggregate match outcomes by league or season; Train model predicting match_result from odds or team features; Compute goal difference statistics

views.name: player_identity
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  player_api_id,
  player_name,
  player_fifa_api_id,
  birthday,
  height,
  weight
FROM Player

params.description: Provides one-row-per-player identity and static attributes (IDs, name, FIFA id, birthdate, height, weight) from the Player table.
params.when_to_use: Look up a player's canonical identifiers and static profile attributes by player id or API id. | Join player identity to other game-level or attribute-level datasets to add player name or birthdate. | Compose with analytics that need player-level demographic fields (age, height, weight) as dimensions or grouping keys.
params.output_schema: id: Surrogate primary key for the player row — derived directly from Player.id | player_api_id: External API identifier for the player — derived directly from Player.player_api_id | player_name: The player's full name as recorded — derived directly from Player.player_name | player_fifa_api_id: FIFA-specific player identifier (may be null) — derived directly from Player.player_fifa_api_id | birthday: The player's date of birth (date) — derived directly from Player.birthday | height: Player height (numeric, units as recorded in source) — derived directly from Player.height | weight: Player weight (numeric, units as recorded in source) — derived directly from Player.weight
params.grounded_columns: Player.id | Player.player_api_id | Player.player_name | Player.player_fifa_api_id | Player.birthday | Player.height | Player.weight
params.metric: No derived aggregate metrics are produced by this view; all outputs are direct column projections. Example expressions you can compute after joining: age = DATE_PART('year', CURRENT_DATE) - DATE_PART('year', birthday) (user-defined, not in view).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to player_latest_attributes on player_latest_attributes.player_id = player_identity.id — safe because player_identity is one-row-per-id and player_latest_attributes (a RANK sibling) should also be one-row-per-player when materialized as 'latest'; this will not duplicate player_identity rows when both are one-row-per-player. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to match_lineup_players_unpivot on match_lineup_players_unpivot.player_id = player_identity.id — NOT safe unless match_lineup_players_unpivot is explicitly aggregated or filtered to one-row-per-player-per-match and you expect that multiplicity. match_lineup_players_unpivot is a one-to-many (many lineups / matches per player) reshape — joining directly will multiply player_identity rows by each lineup occurrence. To preserve player-level cardinality, aggregate match occurrences first (for example, COUNT(match_id) grouped by player_id) then join the aggregated result to player_identity. | cardinality-SAFE guidance: join to match_basic_outcomes on player_identity.id = match_basic_outcomes.player_id — NOT safe to keep player-level uniqueness because match_basic_outcomes is a normalized events/match-level table (one-to-many). Aggregate metrics (goals, appearances) in match_basic_outcomes grouped by player_id before joining to avoid duplicating player_identity rows. | cardinality-SAFE guidance: join to match_team_odds on player_identity.id = match_team_odds.player_id — NOT safe unless match_team_odds is pre-aggregated by player or limited to one row per player; otherwise it will multiply player_identity rows because odds are match/team-level measures (one-to-many). | General rule: This view is strictly a dimension-like one-row-per-player table. It is safe to join directly to other dimension-like, one-row-per-player views (e.g., a properly defined player_latest_attributes) on the player id keys without causing duplication. Do not directly join it to event/match/lineup-level tables (one-to-many) without first aggregating those tables to player-level metrics (COUNT, SUM, AVG grouped by player_id) or otherwise restricting to a single row per player.

views.description: Core player identity table (one row per Player) to join human-readable player_name and birthday onto other relations like appearances or attributes. Keeps both player_api_id and player_fifa_api_id for safe joins to either key. | Use for: Lookup player_name and birthday for appearances; Compute age at match date by joining to match date; Filter players by height/weight or name

views.name: match_team_odds
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  match_api_id,
  home_team_api_id,
  away_team_api_id,
  B365H,
  B365D,
  B365A,
  ( (CASE WHEN B365H IS NOT NULL THEN B365H ELSE NULL END) +
    (CASE WHEN BWH IS NOT NULL THEN BWH ELSE 0 END) +
    (CASE WHEN IWH IS NOT NULL THEN IWH ELSE 0 END)
  ) / ( (CASE WHEN B365H IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) + (CASE WHEN BWH IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) + (CASE WHEN IWH IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) ) AS mean_home_odds
FROM Match

params.description: Per-match row of selected betting odds and a computed mean of available home-win odds — answers questions about match-level bookmaker odds and a simple averaged home-win price.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve bookmaker odds (Bet365 home/draw/away) for a specific match (by id or match_api_id). | Compare home-side odds across matches or teams. | Compose further match-level metrics that use per-match odds (e.g., merge with match outcomes to compute implied probabilities). | Join odds to one-row-per-match dimensions (team, competition, season) without needing additional aggregation.
params.output_schema: id: primary key of the Match row (Match.id) — one row per match in this view. | match_api_id: external match identifier from Match.match_api_id. | home_team_api_id: home team external identifier from Match.home_team_api_id. | away_team_api_id: away team external identifier from Match.away_team_api_id. | B365H: Bet365 decimal odds for a home win, from Match.B365H (NULL if not recorded). | B365D: Bet365 decimal odds for a draw, from Match.B365D (NULL if not recorded). | B365A: Bet365 decimal odds for an away win, from Match.B365A (NULL if not recorded). | mean_home_odds: mean of available home-win odds across three bookmakers (B365H, BWH, IWH) computed per the expression below; NULL when B365H is NULL and no other contributing terms are present per the expression's denominator logic.
params.grounded_columns: Match.id | Match.match_api_id | Match.home_team_api_id | Match.away_team_api_id | Match.B365H | Match.B365D | Match.B365A | Match.BWH | Match.IWH
params.metric: mean_home_odds = ( (CASE WHEN Match.B365H IS NOT NULL THEN Match.B365H ELSE NULL END) + (CASE WHEN Match.BWH IS NOT NULL THEN Match.BWH ELSE 0 END) + (CASE WHEN Match.IWH IS NOT NULL THEN Match.IWH ELSE 0 END) ) / ( (CASE WHEN Match.B365H IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) + (CASE WHEN Match.BWH IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) + (CASE WHEN Match.IWH IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) ) | Note: expression treats B365H specially by placing NULL (which behaves like adding NULL) when B365H IS NULL — functionally this causes the numerator to be NULL if B365H is NULL while still counting BWH and IWH in numerator as 0 when absent. The denominator counts only non-NULL contributors among B365H, BWH, IWH.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to one-row-per-match or one-row-per-team dimensions on the listed keys — these joins will not duplicate measures. | Safe: join to match_basic_outcomes on Match.id = match_basic_outcomes.id — safe because both are one-row-per-match (AGG/NORM views aligned to the match id), so mean_home_odds will not be duplicated. | Safe: join to team_latest_attributes on home_team_api_id = team_latest_attributes.team_api_id (or away_team_api_id = team_latest_attributes.team_api_id) — safe when team_latest_attributes is one-row-per-team (RANK) so joining on team_api_id does not multiply match rows. | Safe: join to player_identity only when joining on a one-to-one key (e.g., if you only attach a single player-level identifier per match via a pre-aggregated key). | Do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables or views without re-aggregation: examples include match_lineup_players_unpivot (RESHAPE) which has many players per match. Joining this view directly to match_lineup_players_unpivot on id will multiply match rows by number of lineup players and thus will duplicate mean_home_odds and other per-match measures. Instead, either: | - aggregate the one-to-many side to one row per match (e.g., count players per match) before joining, or | - join and then re-aggregate results back to match grain, using SUM/AVG on measures that are intended to be combined, and ensuring measures from this view are not double-counted. | Do NOT join to sibling views that are at a finer grain (e.g., player_latest_attributes) without first reducing that sibling to match-level keys. Any join that maps one row in this view to multiple rows in the other side will multiply per-match measures. | When composing additional metrics: treat this view's outputs as match-grain base measures. If your downstream query needs per-team-season aggregations, aggregate mean_home_odds appropriately (e.g., AVG(mean_home_odds) grouped by team and season) after joining only to safe dimensions or after pre-aggregating one-to-many details.

views.description: Aggregate betting-odds measures at the match level selecting available bookie odds into median-like measures. Provides B365 and a simple mean_odds across available bookmakers (ignores NULLs). Useful for studies comparing implied probabilities vs outcomes. | Use for: Compare odds to match outcomes; Filter matches by odds ranges; Use mean odds as feature in prediction
